headline: Inside Higher Ed Calls AI's Evidence Base 'Nonexistent' as Vendors and Districts Race Ahead Anyway
thesis: A new Inside Higher Ed report finds almost no independent research on whether AI actually improves learning, even as vendors ship AI-native platforms and schools write new AI and screen-time rules for the year ahead.
summary: Inside Higher Ed leads with MIT researcher Justin Reich's warning that the evidence base for AI's educational benefits is "almost nonexistent," even as colleges sign multimillion-dollar AI contracts faster than independent research can evaluate them. That gap between deployment and evidence runs through the rest of today's coverage: EdTech Magazine details a new hybrid-cloud infrastructure guide for K-12 IT teams, THE Journal's archive shows Renaissance and Kiddom continuing to push all-in-one 'Education Intelligence' and AI-instruction platforms, and EdSurge reports AI-generated video content is warping early learning according to teachers on the ground. On governance, Education Technology Insights' CXO column argues for a strategic, ethics-first approach to AI adoption, while EdTech Digest's guest column on 'reindustrializing' the classroom makes a similar case for deliberate, human-centered technology use. Screen time remains a live equity issue: Brookings' new survey finds parents and teens broadly support school cellphone bans and don't perceive major downsides a year in, echoing THE Journal's coverage of CoSN's push for purpose-based screen-time policy over blanket limits. Equity questions extend further as EdSurge reports parents are bringing AI tools into IEP meetings and EdTech Magazine explores what brain-computer interfaces could mean for students with disabilities. The fall conference calendar is about to open in earnest: 1EdTech's Learning Impact Europe convenes in Thessaloniki starting tomorrow, ISTE+ASCD's Edtech Leader Certification cohort enrollment closes September 17, and EdTech Week, the StartEd CEO Summit and Ed-Fi's Alliance Summit follow in October and November.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · September 14, 2026 · Items were sourced and dated via web-search indexing rather than live page fetches this run (direct fetches to source sites were blocked by network egress restrictions); Education Technology Insights, EdTech Week and Ed-Fi Alliance had no September-dated coverage surface in search, so their most relevant recent items are listed instead with a note.

themes.title: The Research Gap Behind AI's Rapid Classroom Rollout
themes.body: Inside Higher Ed reports MIT's Justin Reich calling the evidence base for AI's educational benefits "almost nonexistent," even as colleges and vendors race ahead of independent research on what actually works.

themes.title: Vendors Keep Shipping AI-Native Platforms Ahead of the Evidence

themes.title: A Case for Slower, More Deliberate AI Adoption
themes.body: Education Technology Insights' CXO column argues for a strategic, ethics-first approach to responsible AI, and EdTech Digest's guest column on 'reindustrializing' the classroom makes a parallel case for intentional, human-centered technology use.

themes.title: A Year In, Parents and Teens Warm to Cellphone Bans
